Credential Management.hook: Every login is a door into the firm: **give the smallest key** that works
points: Admin, Editor, Viewer: assign **the minimum role** the job needs
Admin only for whoever is **directly responsible** for the system
**MFA on every account**, no matter how routine
**Review roles periodically**, not just at setup
Credential Management.scene: A new team member at Thorne & Partners will **update shared documents** but never touch settings. Someone suggests Admin access.
Credential Management.move: Grant **Editor, not Admin**; expand only if a real need surfaces
dos: Document **who has which role** and why

Least-Privilege Access.hook: Over-permissioning is how systems **get broken by people with no bad intent**
points: Grant access for **what the role needs**, not someday-convenience
Spot extra access? **Flag it for correction** now
After an incident, **fix the role, not blame**
Temporary access **ends when the need ends**
Least-Privilege Access.scene: A junior staffer mistakenly given **admin access** modified system settings they never should have been able to touch.
Least-Privilege Access.move: **Correct the role**, then review who else is over-permissioned
dos: Treat the fix as **correcting the role**
donts: Don't leave excess access **because nothing broke yet**

Multi-Factor Authentication Basics.hook: A password alone is **a single point of failure**
points: MFA: something you know **plus something you have**
Turn MFA on for **every sensitive account**
**Email comes first**: it can reset other passwords
Prefer **an authenticator app or hardware key** over SMS
Multi-Factor Authentication Basics.scene: Checking your accounts, you find an older email account set up **before MFA was required** and never updated.
Multi-Factor Authentication Basics.move: **Enable MFA now**, with an authenticator app over SMS
donts: Don't skip **older accounts** set up pre-MFA
Don't **default to SMS codes** when options exist

Password Manager Best Practices.hook: Reuse one password and **one breach becomes a breach everywhere**
points: **A unique password** for every account, generated by the manager
Guard the **master password** hardest: it unlocks everything
Share through **the built-in sharing feature**, password hidden
Compromise suspected? **Change the password immediately**
Password Manager Best Practices.scene: You find firm passwords **in an unencrypted note**, and a colleague asks you to email one over.
Password Manager Best Practices.move: Move them into the manager; **share via its built-in feature**
donts: Never send passwords **in plain-text email or chat**
Don't **wait to see** if something goes wrong

Shared Account Risks.hook: A shared login **erases accountability** the moment something goes wrong
points: Shared login: **no way to know** who acted
Offboarding one person means **changing everyone's password**
**Individual, scoped accounts** are almost always safer
A shared account is **a known risk to manage**
Shared Account Risks.scene: A setting in a shared firm account was changed, and several people use the same login. **Nobody can say who** did it.
Shared Account Risks.move: Push for **individual, scoped accounts**; until then, log every use
dos: **Log who used** a shared account for what
Ask if it **could be individual accounts**
donts: Don't treat shared logins as **low-maintenance convenience**
Don't let **a leaver keep** the password

Offboarding Access Removal Checklist.hook: When someone leaves, **every system** they touched gets revoked, not just email
points: Keep **a written checklist**: every system, account, shared credential
Work the **full list for every departure**
**Revoke on the departure date**, not later
Add each **new system to the list** right away
Offboarding Access Removal Checklist.line: 'Probably fine to leave active for now' is **exactly the stale permission** to prevent
Offboarding Access Removal Checklist.scene: A contractor's work with the firm ends Friday. Email gets shut off, but they also used **a shared login** and a smaller, less obvious tool.
Offboarding Access Removal Checklist.move: Run **the full checklist** and change the shared credential that day
dos: List **every system**, not just obvious ones
donts: Don't stop at **the systems that come to mind**

The Golden Rules of Admin Data Security.hook: An AI tool is **still a third party**: confidentiality goes with you
points: **Toggle off training settings** before any real work
Never input **financial data, health info, SSNs, or passwords**
Swap real names for **placeholders like '[Company X]'**
Unsure if it's safe? **Treat it as unsafe**
The Golden Rules of Admin Data Security.line: The judgment that keeps case details out of conversation **applies to every prompt**
The Golden Rules of Admin Data Security.scene: You want an AI tool's help drafting a real **termination email** full of names and identifying details.
The Golden Rules of Admin Data Security.move: Settings off, then **swap every name for placeholders** before pasting
dos: Treat AI like **any outside third party**
donts: Don't relax **because the task seems routine**

Classifying Information by Sensitivity L.hook: Classify before you share: **the level sets the handling**
points: **Public**: fine to share freely, once confirmed it's meant for outside
**Internal**: not secret, but not for outside distribution
**Confidential / Privileged**: case details, client communications, financial data
Unsure? **Treat it as more sensitive** until confirmed
Classifying Information by Sensitivity L.scene: An outside contact asks for **an internal memo** that isn't secret but was never meant for outside distribution.
Classifying Information by Sensitivity L.move: Classify it **Internal**: it stays inside unless confirmed otherwise
dos: **Confirm Public is truly public** before sharing

Secure File Sharing Methods.hook: Once an attachment is sent, **you lose control** of where it goes
points: Use **an access-controlled link** over an email attachment
Set **expiration dates and permissions** on every link
Send the password **through a separate channel**
**Revoke the link** once it's no longer needed
Secure File Sharing Methods.scene: You need to send a sensitive file outside the firm and plan to put **the file and its password** in one email.
Secure File Sharing Methods.move: Send **a secure, expiring link**; password by a separate channel
dos: Confirm the recipient **actually needs the file**
**Set an expiry** on every shared link

Email Encryption Basics.hook: Standard email **isn't inherently secure**; privileged content needs more
points: **Privileged legal content** usually needs encryption
Not everything needs encryption: **judge each message**
Check for **your firm's encrypted option**; many go unused
Encryption is **a layer, not a replacement** for judgment
Email Encryption Basics.scene: You're about to send **privileged legal content** to a client by standard email.
Email Encryption Basics.move: Use **the encrypted email option**; unsure? Encrypt anyway
dos: First ask **whether it should be sent**
donts: Don't **encrypt everything** that feels vaguely important

Metadata Risks in Shared Documents.hook: A document that **looks clean** can still carry its full edit history
points: Metadata leaks: **track changes, comments, author names, past edits**
**Clean it explicitly** before any external share
Extra care for **anything going to opposing counsel**
**Verify the clean version** before you send
Metadata Risks in Shared Documents.scene: A draft is going to opposing counsel. On screen it looks clean, but **an internal comment** is still in the file.
Metadata Risks in Shared Documents.move: Remove changes and comments, then **verify nothing hidden remains**
dos: Make **the clean export standard**, not occasional

Redaction Done Right.hook: If hidden text can be **copied, searched or uncovered**, it wasn't redacted
points: A black box only covers text; **real redaction deletes it**
In Acrobat, **apply the redactions** after marking them
Federal filings: **last four digits** of SSNs and account numbers
Birth year only, minor's initials only; **the attorney decides** the rest
Redaction Done Right.line: The attorney checks every redacted file **before it's filed or sent**
Redaction Done Right.scene: You must file a client's bank statement as an exhibit. It shows **the full account number**, a birth date and their child's full name.
Redaction Done Right.move: Redact to **last four, birth year, initials**; then test it
dos: Redact **the same detail everywhere**, including file names
donts: Never **black-highlight in Word** then save as PDF
Never send **the original alongside** the redacted file

Device Security Fundamentals.hook: An unlocked device, even briefly, is **an open door**
points: Short screen-lock timeout, and **lock manually** before stepping away
**Full-disk encryption** turns a lost laptop into a hardware loss
Personal phones for work carry **the same confidentiality obligations**
**Patch promptly** and set up remote wipe
Device Security Fundamentals.scene: Between meetings you check Elias's email on **your personal phone**, then leave it unlocked on the table.
Device Security Fundamentals.move: Treat it like a work device: **lock, encrypt, patch**

Physical Security Basics.hook: Physical access is still access: **lock what you leave**
points: **Lock your laptop** whenever you step away
**Lock filing cabinets** overnight and when unattended
Lost badge or key? **Report it immediately**, like a password
Visitors and vendors get **a clear, limited area**
Physical Security Basics.scene: Monday morning your office access card is missing. You're tempted to **mention it eventually**.
Physical Security Basics.move: **Report the lost card now**, as urgently as a compromised password
dos: **Check your workspace** for visible sensitive items
donts: Don't wait to **report a lost badge**

Clean Desk Policy.hook: A document left on a desk is **a physical data leak**
points: **Put sensitive papers away** between tasks
**Check the printer tray** after printing anything sensitive
An unlocked screen is **a document left out**
**Home workspaces** follow the same rules
Clean Desk Policy.scene: You print Elias's notes for a client meeting, get pulled into a call and **leave them in the printer tray**.
Clean Desk Policy.move: **Collect prints immediately**, and do an end-of-day desk check
dos: **End each day** with a desk check

Secure Disposal of Sensitive Documents.hook: Trash isn't disposal: **shredding destroys the information**
points: **Shred sensitive paper**, never regular trash or recycling
Deleting a file isn't enough: **use secure deletion**
**Shred on a schedule**: end of day or week
**Drafts and working copies** get shredded too
Secure Disposal of Sensitive Documents.scene: Printed drafts of a confidential memo have **piled up by your desk** all week, headed for recycling.
Secure Disposal of Sensitive Documents.move: **Shred them now**, and make it a weekly habit

Litigation Holds: When Nothing Can Be De.hook: Once a lawsuit is reasonably expected, **nothing relevant gets deleted**
points: A hold starts when a suit is **reasonably expected**, not filed
It **overrides normal clean-up** and retention schedules
Emails, texts, chats, drafts, calendars, voicemails, paper: **all count**
Losing held information, even by accident, is **spoliation**
Litigation Holds: When Nothing Can Be De.line: Keep the hold until **the attorney releases it in writing**
Litigation Holds: When Nothing Can Be De.scene: Harlow Industries gets a lawsuit threat. That week **the annual shred starts**, and a departing employee's laptop is due to be wiped Friday.
Litigation Holds: When Nothing Can Be De.move: **Stop the shred and the wipe**; loop in the attorney and IT
dos: **Send reminders on a schedule**, e.g. quarterly
donts: Never **tidy up old emails** during a case

Fixing a Broken Workflow.hook: Disconnected tools **reliably cause duplicate work**, even among careful people
points: Spot workflows split across **email, spreadsheet and notes**
**Consolidate into one tracked system** where task state lives
**Name which steps stay manual**, deliberately
**Test on a real task** before fully committing
Fixing a Broken Workflow.scene: Requests for Elias are tracked across email, a spreadsheet and personal notes, and **the same task gets done twice**.
Fixing a Broken Workflow.move: Move it to **one tracked system**; name the manual steps
dos: **Make each manual step** a deliberate choice
**Revisit after use** to confirm the fix

points: **Manufactured urgency** is a red flag, not a reason to skip checks
Verify claimed authority **through a known, separate channel**
**New payment method or unfamiliar account**? Take a second look
**Report attempts** even when you didn't fall for them
Social Engineering Red Flags.scene: A caller claiming to be from IT says Elias is locked out and **needs access right now**, with no time to verify.
Social Engineering Red Flags.move: Hang up and **call IT on a known number**
dos: **Report the tactic** so others are warned

Phishing Recognition Beyond Email.hook: Phishing now arrives by **text, call and calendar invite** too
points: **Same skepticism** for texts, calls and invites as email
Tells: **generic greeting, off sender, unexpected attachment**
Verify via **a number you already know**
**An unusual channel** makes a request more suspicious
Phishing Recognition Beyond Email.scene: A text with a generic greeting, claiming to be from a vendor, asks you to call **the number in the message**.
Phishing Recognition Beyond Email.move: Ignore that number; **call one you already know**
dos: **Report it**, whatever channel it came through
donts: Never **use contact details from** the suspicious message

Recognizing Insider Threat Warning Signs.hook: Not every risk comes from outside: **notice access that doesn't fit**
points: Watch for **access that doesn't match** someone's role
Most insider incidents are **well-meaning shortcuts**, not sabotage
It's **a system observation**, not a personal accusation
**Fix the process gap** whatever the intent
Recognizing Insider Threat Warning Signs.line: **Flag it to the right person**; never confront a colleague directly
Recognizing Insider Threat Warning Signs.scene: You notice a colleague regularly opening files from matters **outside their role**.
Recognizing Insider Threat Warning Signs.move: **Flag the access pattern** to the appropriate person, without accusing

Responding to a Suspicious Data Request.hook: A suspicious request gets three moves: **verify, escalate, close the gap**
points: **Verify the sender's identity** before anything else
**Escalate through the correct** internal channel
**Close the gap** that let it reach you
Responding to a Suspicious Data Request.scene: An email that appears to come from David Reyes asks you to send **a client file** to an unfamiliar address.
Responding to a Suspicious Data Request.move: **Verify with David directly**, then escalate before sending anything
dos: **Fix the gap**, not just the request
donts: Don't **handle it solo** outside the channel

The First 10 Minutes of a Security Incid.hook: In the first 10 minutes: **contain, assess, notify, document**
points: **Contain first**: disconnect, revoke access or pause the leak
**Assess** what's exposed and to whom, as precisely as you can
**Notify immediately**; don't wait for the complete picture
**Document in real time**; early memory fades fast
The First 10 Minutes of a Security Incid.scene: You realize a sharing link to **a confidential file** has been open to anyone, and you don't know who has seen it.
The First 10 Minutes of a Security Incid.move: **Revoke the link now**, then notify before you know everything

Containing a Confidentiality Leak.hook: In a leak, **containment comes before anything else**
points: **Contain the spread** immediately
Notify **the right roles**, not just the right names
Put **a policy in place** so it can't repeat
Containing a Confidentiality Leak.scene: A confidential case update went to **the wrong distribution list**, and replies are already coming in.
Containing a Confidentiality Leak.move: **Stop the spread first**, then alert the right roles
dos: **Notify by role**, not just by name
donts: Don't stop at **whoever comes to mind**

Who to Notify and When.hook: Know **who gets told** before an incident, not during one
points: Different incidents, **different people and timelines**
A real data breach may carry **legal notification obligations**
Map incidents to contacts: **IT, a partner, outside counsel**
Uncertain? **Escalate to someone senior**
Who to Notify and When.line: Never decide alone it's **not serious enough to mention**
Who to Notify and When.scene: A possible data breach surfaces, and you realize **you've never confirmed** who the right contact is.
Who to Notify and When.move: **Escalate to someone senior now**; confirm contacts before the next one

Documenting an Incident as It Unfolds.hook: A real-time record **beats a reconstruction** written days later
points: Log **what happened, when**, and what actions were taken
**Timestamps and short facts** beat a polished summary
Record **who was notified** and when
**Facts, not blame**; preserve the log afterward
Documenting an Incident as It Unfolds.scene: Mid-incident, Elias asks when IT was told. You're relying on memory, and **details have started to blur**.
Documenting an Incident as It Unfolds.move: Keep **a timestamped log** from the first minute onward
dos: **Write it as it happens**; rough is fine
**Preserve the log** for review and compliance
donts: Don't **wait to write** a polished summary

Post-Incident Review.hook: A real review **stops the same failure repeating** in another form
points: Cover **what happened, what worked, what should change**
Focus on **the process gap**, not the individual
Base it on **the real-time documentation**
Leave with **one concrete change**
Post-Incident Review.line: **Blame-focused reviews** make people less likely to report the next issue
Post-Incident Review.scene: The incident is resolved and everyone wants to move on. **Nobody has scheduled a review**, and it's quietly closing out.
Post-Incident Review.move: Run the review and **capture one concrete change**

Crisis Communication Principles.hook: In a crisis, communicate **calm, factual and frequent**
points: **Silence or vague reassurance** raises anxiety
Share only **what's confirmed**, clearly labeled
Use ACT: **Acknowledge, Clarify, Timeline**
**Confirm updates reach** everyone who needs them
Crisis Communication Principles.scene: During an incident, staff keep asking what's happening. You're tempted to say **everything's fine** before anything is confirmed.
Crisis Communication Principles.move: Acknowledge it, clarify unknowns, **give the next update time**
donts: Don't **go quiet** waiting for the full picture

Maintaining Calm Under Pressure.hook: Your visible calm is **often the only calm** in the room
points: Calm is **contagious**, and so is panic
Calm isn't passive: **think clearly, act deliberately**
**Pause a few seconds** before responding
**Practice your technique** before a real crisis
Maintaining Calm Under Pressure.scene: A crisis breaks and everyone around you is reacting. They're all watching **how you respond**.
Maintaining Calm Under Pressure.move: **Pause a few seconds**, then act deliberately

Chain of Command During a Crisis.hook: Know **who decides what** before the crisis, not during it
points: Use **the Day 1 Command Hierarchy** in a crisis too
Know **the real backup** for each escalation point
**Escalate through the chain**, even under time pressure
**Check backups are current**; roles change quietly
Chain of Command During a Crisis.scene: A crisis needs a decision now, and Elias is **unreachable on a flight** to London.
Chain of Command During a Crisis.move: Go straight to **the backup you identified in advance**
donts: Don't **improvise a new process** under pressure
Don't **skip steps** because it feels faster

Business Continuity Basics.hook: Plan **before you need it**: what if something critical vanished tomorrow?
points: List **critical systems, key contacts, backup options**
It **doesn't need to be elaborate** to be useful
Find your **single points of failure**
**Revisit the plan** as the work changes
Business Continuity Basics.scene: The one person who knows how to run **a critical system** is suddenly unavailable, and there's no backup plan.
Business Continuity Basics.move: Name a backup for **every single point of failure**
dos: **Name a backup** for each critical item

Crisis PR & Media Containment.hook: Media crises move fast: the window is **minutes, not hours**
points: Confirm **who's authorized to speak** before it's needed
Use **a prepared holding statement**, never silence or improvising
Escalate to communications, legal, the executive **in parallel**
Crisis PR & Media Containment.line: Never respond to media **outside the authorization chain**, even to help
Crisis PR & Media Containment.scene: A journalist calls you directly, bypassing the firm's usual channels, asking for **comment on a sensitive matter**.
Crisis PR & Media Containment.move: Give **the holding line**, then alert Priya Nair and Elias immediately
dos: Say **no comment, here's who to contact**
**Escalate in parallel**, not one by one

Attorney-Client Privilege: What EAs Need.hook: You sit inside the privileged relationship, so **the duty extends to you**
points: Privilege protects **lawyer-client communications for legal advice**
**The wrong recipient** on a thread can waive it
Never discuss case details **where they could be overheard**
Unsure? **Ask the attorney directly**
Attorney-Client Privilege: What EAs Need.line: An accidental disclosure **can't be undone** once it happens
Attorney-Client Privilege: What EAs Need.scene: Replying on Elias's privileged thread with a client, autocomplete adds **someone outside the relationship**.
Attorney-Client Privilege: What EAs Need.move: **Check the recipient list** before sending; remove them
dos: Treat legal-advice communications **as privileged by default**

Work-Product Confidentiality.hook: Strategy memos and case analysis carry **their own protection**
points: Work product covers **the attorney's thought process** and preparation
**Careless handling can waive it**, even without client communications
**Handle it like privileged material**
**Label and store it clearly** in the document system
Work-Product Confidentiality.line: Never share work product **outside the matter team** without explicit confirmation
Work-Product Confidentiality.scene: A colleague on an unrelated matter asks to see **a strategy memo** from a case you support, to think through a similar issue.
Work-Product Confidentiality.move: **Don't share it**; get explicit confirmation from the matter team first
dos: **Treat it as protected** when in doubt

Investor Disclosure Confidentiality.hook: Investors get **only what's been cleared**, nothing more
points: **Confirm it's cleared** before any investor communication
Store investor materials in **access-controlled storage**
Requests beyond cleared material: **escalate, don't answer**
Investor info sits in **the highly restricted tier**
Investor Disclosure Confidentiality.line: Answering beyond cleared material is **not a solo judgment call**
Investor Disclosure Confidentiality.scene: An investor emails asking for details on **an ongoing matter** that hasn't been publicly disclosed.
Investor Disclosure Confidentiality.move: **Escalate the request**; confirm what's cleared before replying
dos: **Keep investor files separate** from internal documents
donts: Don't treat investors as **entitled to everything**

HIPAA in a Legal Context.hook: When a case file **touches medical records**, HIPAA comes with it
points: Watch for **personal injury, workers' comp, disability** matters
A firm **needn't be a healthcare provider** for HIPAA to matter
Share medical records **only with those who need them**
Health information defaults to **the highest sensitivity tier**
HIPAA in a Legal Context.scene: A workers' compensation matter arrives with **medical records** in the case file.
HIPAA in a Legal Context.move: Classify it **highest tier**; share only with who needs it
donts: Don't assume **HIPAA is only for healthcare**

GDPR & Data Privacy Regulations.hook: GDPR can apply **even if the firm isn't in the EU**
points: It covers **personal data of individuals in the EU**
People can **know what's held** and often request deletion
U.S. state laws like **California's CCPA** work similarly
Check for **non-U.S. personal data** at intake
GDPR & Data Privacy Regulations.line: Data privacy is **never someone else's concern**: flag it early
GDPR & Data Privacy Regulations.scene: A new matter includes **personal data belonging to EU individuals**, and nobody has raised privacy obligations.
GDPR & Data Privacy Regulations.move: **Flag it to the attorney early**, at intake
dos: **Organize records** with data rights in mind
donts: Don't assume **not in the EU means exempt**
Don't **memorize every rule**; recognize the trigger

Other Relevant Compliance Frameworks.hook: The skill is **pattern recognition**, not memorizing every statute
points: Health, financial, minors', foreign data carry **extra regulatory weight**
**SOX** for public-company financial records
**GLBA and FERPA**: financial data and education records
**State bar ethics rules** reach beyond privilege
Other Relevant Compliance Frameworks.line: Unfamiliar regulatory area? **Ask the attorney**; never guess the requirement
Other Relevant Compliance Frameworks.scene: A new matter for a public company involves **its financial records**, and you're unsure which rules apply.
Other Relevant Compliance Frameworks.move: Apply extra care and **ask the attorney about obligations**
dos: **Default to extra care** for sensitive categories
donts: Don't treat privilege as **the only confidentiality duty**
